[120](https://docs.rs#120)/// Represents a contiguous piece of a single allocation with some layout that is used as a
[121](https://docs.rs#121)/// data copying destination. May be wholly or partially uninitialized.
[122](https://docs.rs#122)///
[123](https://docs.rs#123)/// This trait is *basically* equivalent to implementing `Deref`/`DerefMut` with
[124](https://docs.rs#124)/// `Target = [MaybeUninit<u8>]` in terms of safety requirements. It is a separate
[125](https://docs.rs#125)/// trait for the extra flexibility having a trait we own provides: namely, the ability
[126](https://docs.rs#126)/// to implement it on foreign types.
[127](https://docs.rs#127)///
[128](https://docs.rs#128)/// # Safety
[129](https://docs.rs#129)///
[130](https://docs.rs#130)/// Implementors of this trait must ensure these guarantees:
[131](https://docs.rs#131)///
[132](https://docs.rs#132)/// - The memory range represented by `base_ptr` and `size` **may** be wholly or partially uninitialized
[133](https://docs.rs#133)/// - `base_ptr` **must** point to a valid, single allocation of at least `size` bytes.
[134](https://docs.rs#134)/// - `size` **must not** be greater than `isize::MAX`
[135](https://docs.rs#135)///
[136](https://docs.rs#136)/// Assume the lifetime of a shared borrow of self is named `'a`:
[137](https://docs.rs#137)///
[138](https://docs.rs#138)/// - `base_ptr` **must** be [valid][`core::ptr#safety`] for `'a`
[139](https://docs.rs#139)/// - `base_ptr` **must *not*** be mutably aliased for `'a`
[140](https://docs.rs#140)///     - It is necessary but not sufficient for this requirement that
[141](https://docs.rs#141)/// **no outside *mutable* references** may exist to its data, even if they are unused by user code.
[142](https://docs.rs#142)///
[143](https://docs.rs#143)/// Assume the lifetime of a mutable borrow of self is named `'a`:
[144](https://docs.rs#144)///
[145](https://docs.rs#145)/// - `base_ptr_mut` **must** be [valid][`core::ptr#safety`] for `'a`
[146](https://docs.rs#146)/// - `base_ptr_mut` **must *not*** be aliased at all for `'a`
[147](https://docs.rs#147)///     - It is necessary but not sufficient for this requirement that
[148](https://docs.rs#148)/// **no outside references** may exist to its data, even if they are unused by user code.
[149](https://docs.rs#149)///
[150](https://docs.rs#150)/// Also see the [crate-level safety documentation][`crate#safety`].

[157](https://docs.rs#157)

[217](https://docs.rs#217)    /// implementation for this is still being scaffolded.

[219](https://docs.rs#219)    /// # Safety
[220](https://docs.rs#220)    ///
[221](https://docs.rs#221)    /// Assuming that the safety guarantees for creating `self` were followed,
[222](https://docs.rs#222)    /// the only extra requirement for this to be safe is that **all memory**
[223](https://docs.rs#223)    /// within `range` must be **initialized**. If *any bytes* within
[224](https://docs.rs#224)    /// this range are not initialized, using this function is *instantly **undefined
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    /// behavior***, even if you *do noting* with the result.
[226](https://docs.rs#226)    ///
[227](https://docs.rs#227)    /// Also see the [crate-level Safety documentation][`crate#safety`] for more.
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    unsafe fn assume_range_initialized_as_bytes<R>(&self, range: R) -> &[u8]
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    where
[230](https://docs.rs#230)        R: core::slice::SliceIndex<[MaybeUninit<u8>], Output = [MaybeUninit<u8>]>,
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    {
[232](https://docs.rs#232)        let maybe_uninit_slice = &self.as_maybe_uninit_bytes()[range];
[233](https://docs.rs#233)        // SAFETY: same requirements as function-level safety assuming the requirements
[234](https://docs.rs#234)        // for creating `self` are met since `MaybeUnint<T>` has same layout as `T`
[235](https://docs.rs#235)        unsafe {
[236](https://docs.rs#236)            core::slice::from_raw_parts(
[237](https://docs.rs#237)                maybe_uninit_slice.as_ptr().cast(),
[238](https://docs.rs#238)                maybe_uninit_slice.len(),
[239](https://docs.rs#239)            )
[240](https://docs.rs#240)        }
[241](https://docs.rs#241)    }
[242](https://docs.rs#242)
[243](https://docs.rs#243)    /// Interpret a range of `self` as a mutable byte slice. This assumes that **all bytes**
[244](https://docs.rs#244)    /// within `range` are initialized.
[245](https://docs.rs#245)    ///
[246](https://docs.rs#246)    /// In the future, this will hopefully not be needed as this operation will be equivalent to
[247](https://docs.rs#247)    /// something like `self.as_maybe_uninit_bytes_mut()[range].assume_init()`, but the `core`/`std`
[248](https://docs.rs#248)    /// implementation for this is still being scaffolded.
[249](https://docs.rs#249)    ///
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    /// # Safety
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    ///
[252](https://docs.rs#252)    /// Assuming that the safety guarantees for creating `self` were followed,
[253](https://docs.rs#253)    /// the only extra requirement for this to be safe is that **all memory**
[254](https://docs.rs#254)    /// within `range` must be **initialized**. If *any bytes* within
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    /// this range are not initialized, using this function is *instantly **undefined
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    /// behavior***, even if you *do noting* with the result.
[257](https://docs.rs#257)    ///
[258](https://docs.rs#258)    /// Also see the [crate-level Safety documentation][`crate#safety`] for more.
[259](https://docs.rs#259)    unsafe fn assume_range_initialized_as_bytes_mut<R>(&mut self, range: R) -> &mut [u8]
[260](https://docs.rs#260)    where
[261](https://docs.rs#261)        R: core::slice::SliceIndex<[MaybeUninit<u8>], Output = [MaybeUninit<u8>]>,
[262](https://docs.rs#262)    {
[263](https://docs.rs#263)        let maybe_uninit_slice = &mut self.as_maybe_uninit_bytes_mut()[range];
[264](https://docs.rs#264)        // SAFETY: same requirements as function-level safety assuming the requirements
[265](https://docs.rs#265)        // for creating `self` are met since `MaybeUnint<T>` has same layout as `T`
[266](https://docs.rs#266)        unsafe {
[267](https://docs.rs#267)            core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(
[268](https://docs.rs#268)                maybe_uninit_slice.as_mut_ptr().cast(),
[269](https://docs.rs#269)                maybe_uninit_slice.len(),
[270](https://docs.rs#270)            )
[271](https://docs.rs#271)        }
[272](https://docs.rs#272)    }
[273](https://docs.rs#273)}
[274](https://docs.rs#274)
[275](https://docs.rs#275)// SAFETY: The captured `[MaybeUninit<u8>]` will all be part of the same allocation object, and borrowck
[276](https://docs.rs#276)// will assure that the borrows that occur on `self` on the relevant methods live long enough since they are
[277](https://docs.rs#277)// native borrows anyway.

[285](https://docs.rs#285)    }

[292](https://docs.rs#292)/// Takes a `Vec` and unsafely resizes it to the given length, returning a mutable slice to `MaybeUninit<T>` for each
[293](https://docs.rs#293)/// item in the newly-resized `Vec`.
[294](https://docs.rs#294)///
[295](https://docs.rs#295)/// # Safety
[296](https://docs.rs#296)///
[297](https://docs.rs#297)/// You promise that the given `Vec` already has at least `length` capacity. You also promise to either fill all items before dropping
[298](https://docs.rs#298)/// the returned slice, or to continue to not violate validity rules for any items that you do not initialize.
[299](https://docs.rs#299)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[300](https://docs.rs#300)pub unsafe fn maybe_uninit_slice_from_vec<T>(
[301](https://docs.rs#301)    vec: &mut Vec<T>,

[304](https://docs.rs#304)    // SAFETY: As long as the function-level safety rules are met, this is valid
[305](https://docs.rs#305)    unsafe {
[306](https://docs.rs#306)        #[allow(clippy::uninit_vec)]
[307](https://docs.rs#307)        vec.set_len(length);
[308](https://docs.rs#308)    }
[309](https://docs.rs#309)
[310](https://docs.rs#310)    // SAFETY: If function-level safety is met, then we are constructing a slice within a single allocation. `MaybeUninit<T>` is valid
[311](https://docs.rs#311)    // even for uninit memory, and has the same memory layout as `T`.
[312](https://docs.rs#312)    unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(vec.as_mut_ptr().cast::<MaybeUninit<T>>(), length) }

[315](https://docs.rs#315)/// Copies the elements from `src` to `dst`, returning a mutable reference to the now initialized contents of `dst`.
[316](https://docs.rs#316)///
[317](https://docs.rs#317)/// If `T` does not implement `Copy`, use [`clone_into_maybe_uninit_slice`]
[318](https://docs.rs#318)///
[319](https://docs.rs#319)/// This is similar to [`slice::copy_from_slice`]. This is identical to the implementation of the method
[320](https://docs.rs#320)/// `write_to_slice` on [`MaybeUninit`], but that API is as yet unstable.
[321](https://docs.rs#321)///
[322](https://docs.rs#322)/// # Panics
[323](https://docs.rs#323)///
[324](https://docs.rs#324)/// This function will panic if the two slices have different lengths.
[325](https://docs.rs#325)pub fn copy_into_maybe_uninit_slice<'a, T>(src: &[T], dst: &'a mut [MaybeUninit<T>]) -> &'a mut [T]
[326](https://docs.rs#326)where
[327](https://docs.rs#327)    T: Copy,
[328](https://docs.rs#328){
[329](https://docs.rs#329)    let uninit_src: &[MaybeUninit<T>] =
[330](https://docs.rs#330)        // SAFETY: &[T] and &[MaybeUninit<T>] have the same layout
[331](https://docs.rs#331)        unsafe { &*(src as *const [T] as *const [MaybeUninit<T>]) };
[332](https://docs.rs#332)
[333](https://docs.rs#333)    dst.copy_from_slice(uninit_src);
[334](https://docs.rs#334)
[335](https://docs.rs#335)    // SAFETY: Valid elements have just been copied into `this` so it is initialized
[336](https://docs.rs#336)    unsafe { &mut *(dst as *mut [MaybeUninit<T>] as *mut [T]) }
[337](https://docs.rs#337)}
[338](https://docs.rs#338)
[339](https://docs.rs#339)/// Clones the elements from `src` to `dst`, returning a mutable reference to the now initialized contents of `dst`.
[340](https://docs.rs#340)/// Any already initialized elements will not be dropped.
[341](https://docs.rs#341)///
[342](https://docs.rs#342)/// If `T` implements `Copy`, use [`copy_into_maybe_uninit_slice`]
[343](https://docs.rs#343)///
[344](https://docs.rs#344)/// This is similar to [`slice::clone_from_slice`] but does not drop existing elements. This is identical to the implementation of
[345](https://docs.rs#345)/// the method `write_to_slice_cloned` on [`MaybeUninit`], but that API is as yet unstable.
[346](https://docs.rs#346)///
[347](https://docs.rs#347)/// # Panics
[348](https://docs.rs#348)///
[349](https://docs.rs#349)/// This function will panic if the two slices have different lengths, or if the implementation of `Clone` panics.
[350](https://docs.rs#350)///
[351](https://docs.rs#351)/// If there is a panic, the already cloned elements will be dropped.
[352](https://docs.rs#352)pub fn clone_into_maybe_uninit_slice<'a, T>(src: &[T], dst: &'a mut [MaybeUninit<T>]) -> &'a mut [T]
[353](https://docs.rs#353)where
[354](https://docs.rs#354)    T: Clone,
[355](https://docs.rs#355){
[356](https://docs.rs#356)    // unlike copy_from_slice this does not call clone_from_slice on the slice
[357](https://docs.rs#357)    // this is because `MaybeUninit<T: Clone>` does not implement Clone.
[358](https://docs.rs#358)
[359](https://docs.rs#359)    struct Guard<'a, T> {
[360](https://docs.rs#360)        slice: &'a mut [MaybeUninit<T>],
[361](https://docs.rs#361)        initialized: usize,
[362](https://docs.rs#362)    }
[363](https://docs.rs#363)
[364](https://docs.rs#364)    impl<'a, T> Drop for Guard<'a, T> {
[365](https://docs.rs#365)        fn drop(&mut self) {
[366](https://docs.rs#366)            let initialized_part = &mut self.slice[..self.initialized];
[367](https://docs.rs#367)            // SAFETY: this raw slice will contain only initialized objects
[368](https://docs.rs#368)            // that's why, it is allowed to drop it.
[369](https://docs.rs#369)            unsafe {
[370](https://docs.rs#370)                core::ptr::drop_in_place(
[371](https://docs.rs#371)                    &mut *(initialized_part as *mut [MaybeUninit<T>] as *mut [T]),
[372](https://docs.rs#372)                );
[373](https://docs.rs#373)            }
[374](https://docs.rs#374)        }
[375](https://docs.rs#375)    }
[376](https://docs.rs#376)
[377](https://docs.rs#377)    assert_eq!(
[378](https://docs.rs#378)        dst.len(),
[379](https://docs.rs#379)        src.len(),
[380](https://docs.rs#380)        "destination and source slices have different lengths"
[381](https://docs.rs#381)    );
[382](https://docs.rs#382)    // NOTE: We need to explicitly slice them to the same length
[383](https://docs.rs#383)    // for bounds checking to be elided, and the optimizer will
[384](https://docs.rs#384)    // generate memcpy for simple cases (for example T = u8).
[385](https://docs.rs#385)    let len = dst.len();
[386](https://docs.rs#386)    let src = &src[..len];
[387](https://docs.rs#387)
[388](https://docs.rs#388)    // guard is needed b/c panic might happen during a clone
[389](https://docs.rs#389)    let mut guard = Guard {
[390](https://docs.rs#390)        slice: dst,
[391](https://docs.rs#391)        initialized: 0,
[392](https://docs.rs#392)    };
[393](https://docs.rs#393)
[394](https://docs.rs#394)    #[allow(clippy::needless_range_loop)]
[395](https://docs.rs#395)    for i in 0..len {
[396](https://docs.rs#396)        guard.slice[i].write(src[i].clone());
[397](https://docs.rs#397)        guard.initialized += 1;
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    }
[399](https://docs.rs#399)
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    #[allow(clippy::mem_forget)]
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    core::mem::forget(guard);
[402](https://docs.rs#402)
[403](https://docs.rs#403)    // SAFETY: Valid elements have just been written into `this` so it is initialized
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    unsafe { &mut *(dst as *mut [MaybeUninit<T>] as *mut [T]) }
[405](https://docs.rs#405)}

[464](https://docs.rs#464)unsafe impl<'a> Slab for BorrowedRawAllocation<'a> {

[477](https://docs.rs#477)
[478](https://docs.rs#478)/// Given pointer and offset, returns a new offset aligned to `align`.
[479](https://docs.rs#479)///
[480](https://docs.rs#480)/// `align` *must* be a power of two and >= 1 or else the result is meaningless.
[481](https://docs.rs#481)fn align_offset_up_to(ptr: usize, offset: usize, align: usize) -> Option<usize> {
[482](https://docs.rs#482)    let offsetted_ptr = ptr.checked_add(offset)?;
[483](https://docs.rs#483)    let aligned_ptr = offsetted_ptr.checked_add(align - 1)? & !(align - 1);
[484](https://docs.rs#484)    // don't need to check since we know aligned_ptr is >= ptr at this point
[485](https://docs.rs#485)    Some(aligned_ptr - ptr)
[486](https://docs.rs#486)}
[487](https://docs.rs#487)
[488](https://docs.rs#488)/// Compute and validate offsets for a copy operation with the given parameters.
[489](https://docs.rs#489)fn compute_offsets<S: Slab>(
[490](https://docs.rs#490)    dst: &S,
[491](https://docs.rs#491)    start_offset: usize,
[492](https://docs.rs#492)    t_layout: Layout,
[493](https://docs.rs#493)    min_alignment: usize,
[494](https://docs.rs#494)) -> Result<CopyRecord, CopyError> {
[495](https://docs.rs#495)    let copy_layout = t_layout.align_to(min_alignment.next_power_of_two())?;
[496](https://docs.rs#496)
[497](https://docs.rs#497)    let copy_start_offset =
[498](https://docs.rs#498)        align_offset_up_to(dst.base_ptr() as usize, start_offset, copy_layout.align())
[499](https://docs.rs#499)            .ok_or(CopyError::InvalidLayout)?;
[500](https://docs.rs#500)    let copy_end_offset = copy_start_offset
[501](https://docs.rs#501)        .checked_add(copy_layout.size())
[502](https://docs.rs#502)        .ok_or(CopyError::InvalidLayout)?;
[503](https://docs.rs#503)    let copy_end_offset_padded = copy_start_offset
[504](https://docs.rs#504)        .checked_add(copy_layout.pad_to_align().size())
[505](https://docs.rs#505)        .ok_or(CopyError::InvalidLayout)?;
[506](https://docs.rs#506)
[507](https://docs.rs#507)    // check start is inside slab
[508](https://docs.rs#508)    // if within slab, we also know that copy_start_offset is <= isize::MAX since slab.size() must be <= isize::MAX
[509](https://docs.rs#509)    if copy_start_offset > dst.size() {
[510](https://docs.rs#510)        return Err(CopyError::OffsetOutOfBounds);
[511](https://docs.rs#511)    }
[512](https://docs.rs#512)
[513](https://docs.rs#513)    // check end is inside slab
[514](https://docs.rs#514)    if copy_end_offset_padded > dst.size() {
[515](https://docs.rs#515)        return Err(CopyError::OutOfMemory);
[516](https://docs.rs#516)    }
[517](https://docs.rs#517)
[518](https://docs.rs#518)    Ok(CopyRecord {
[519](https://docs.rs#519)        copy_start_offset,
[520](https://docs.rs#520)        copy_end_offset,
[521](https://docs.rs#521)        copy_end_offset_padded,
[522](https://docs.rs#522)    })
[523](https://docs.rs#523)}
[524](https://docs.rs#524)
[525](https://docs.rs#525)/// An error that may occur during a copy operation.
[526](https://docs.rs#526)#[derive(Debug)]
[527](https://docs.rs#527)pub enum CopyError {
[528](https://docs.rs#528)    /// Copy would exceed the end of the allocation
[529](https://docs.rs#529)    OutOfMemory,
[530](https://docs.rs#530)    /// Requested to copy to an offset outside the bounds of the allocation
[531](https://docs.rs#531)    OffsetOutOfBounds,
[532](https://docs.rs#532)    /// Computed invalid layout for copy operation, probably caused by incredibly large size, offset, or min-alignment parameters
[533](https://docs.rs#533)    InvalidLayout,
[534](https://docs.rs#534)}
[535](https://docs.rs#535)
[536](https://docs.rs#536)impl core::fmt::Display for CopyError {
[537](https://docs.rs#537)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
[538](https://docs.rs#538)        write!(f, "{}", match self {
[539](https://docs.rs#539)            Self::OutOfMemory => "Copy would exceed the end of the allocation",
[540](https://docs.rs#540)            Self::OffsetOutOfBounds => "Requested copy to a location starting outside the allocation",
[541](https://docs.rs#541)            Self::InvalidLayout => "Invalid layout, probably caused by incredibly large size, offset, or alignment parameters",
[542](https://docs.rs#542)        })
[543](https://docs.rs#543)    }
[544](https://docs.rs#544)}
[545](https://docs.rs#545)

[554](https://docs.rs#554)
[555](https://docs.rs#555)/// Record of the results of a copy operation
[556](https://docs.rs#556)#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone)]
[557](https://docs.rs#557)pub struct CopyRecord {
[558](https://docs.rs#558)    /// The offset from the start of the allocation, in bytes, at which the
[559](https://docs.rs#559)    /// copy operation began to write data.
[560](https://docs.rs#560)    ///
[561](https://docs.rs#561)    /// Not necessarily equal to the `start_offset`, since this offset
[562](https://docs.rs#562)    /// includes necessary padding to assure alignment.
[563](https://docs.rs#563)    pub copy_start_offset: usize,
[564](https://docs.rs#564)
[565](https://docs.rs#565)    /// The offset from the start of the allocation, in bytes, at which the
[566](https://docs.rs#566)    /// copy operation no longer wrote data.
[567](https://docs.rs#567)    ///

[625](https://docs.rs#625)    let t_layout = Layout::new::<T>();
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    let record = compute_offsets(&*dst, start_offset, t_layout, min_alignment)?;
[627](https://docs.rs#627)
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    // SAFETY: if compute_offsets succeeded, this has already been checked to be safe.
[629](https://docs.rs#629)    let dst_ptr = unsafe { dst.base_ptr_mut().add(record.copy_start_offset) }.cast::<T>();
[630](https://docs.rs#630)
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    // SAFETY:

[635](https://docs.rs#635)    // of 'a.

[639](https://docs.rs#639)    // - checked that copy stays within bounds of our allocation
[640](https://docs.rs#640)    unsafe {
[641](https://docs.rs#641)        core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(src as *const T, dst_ptr, 1);
[642](https://docs.rs#642)    }

[717](https://docs.rs#717)/// Copies from `src` iterator into the memory represented by `dst` starting at a minimum location
[718](https://docs.rs#718)/// of `start_offset` bytes past the start of `dst`.
[719](https://docs.rs#719)///
[720](https://docs.rs#720)/// Returns a vector of [`CopyRecord`]s, one for each item in the `src` iterator.
[721](https://docs.rs#721)///
[722](https://docs.rs#722)/// - `start_offset` is the offset into the allocation represented by `dst`,
[723](https://docs.rs#723)/// in bytes, before which any copied data will *certainly not* be placed. However,
[724](https://docs.rs#724)/// the actual beginning of the copied data may not be exactly at `start_offset` if
[725](https://docs.rs#725)/// padding bytes are needed to satisfy alignment requirements. The actual beginning
[726](https://docs.rs#726)/// of the copied bytes is contained in the returned [`CopyRecord`]s.
[727](https://docs.rs#727)/// - `min_alignment` is the minimum alignment to which the copy will be aligned. The
[728](https://docs.rs#728)/// copy may not actually be aligned to `min_alignment` depending on the alignment requirements
[729](https://docs.rs#729)/// of `T`.
[730](https://docs.rs#730)/// - For this variation, `min_alignment` will also be respected *between* elements yielded by
[731](https://docs.rs#731)/// the iterator. To copy inner elements aligned only to `align_of::<T>()`, see
[732](https://docs.rs#732)/// [`copy_from_iter_to_offset_with_align_packed`]
[733](https://docs.rs#733)///
[734](https://docs.rs#734)/// # Safety
[735](https://docs.rs#735)///
[736](https://docs.rs#736)/// This function is safe on its own, however it is very possible to do unsafe
[737](https://docs.rs#737)/// things if you read the copied data in the wrong way. See the
[738](https://docs.rs#738)/// [crate-level Safety documentation][`crate#safety`] for more.
[739](https://docs.rs#739)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[740](https://docs.rs#740)pub fn copy_from_iter_to_offset_with_align<T: Copy, Iter: Iterator<Item = T>, S: Slab>(
[741](https://docs.rs#741)    src: Iter,
[742](https://docs.rs#742)    dst: &mut S,
[743](https://docs.rs#743)    start_offset: usize,
[744](https://docs.rs#744)    min_alignment: usize,
[745](https://docs.rs#745)) -> Result<Vec<CopyRecord>, CopyError> {
[746](https://docs.rs#746)    let mut offset = start_offset;
[747](https://docs.rs#747)
[748](https://docs.rs#748)    src.map(|item| {
[749](https://docs.rs#749)        let copy_record = copy_to_offset_with_align(&item, dst, offset, min_alignment)?;
[750](https://docs.rs#750)        offset = copy_record.copy_end_offset;
[751](https://docs.rs#751)        Ok(copy_record)
[752](https://docs.rs#752)    })
[753](https://docs.rs#753)    .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
[754](https://docs.rs#754)}
[755](https://docs.rs#755)
[756](https://docs.rs#756)/// Like [`copy_from_iter_to_offset_with_align`] except that
[757](https://docs.rs#757)/// alignment between elements yielded by the iterator will ignore `min_alignment`
[758](https://docs.rs#758)/// and rather only be aligned to the alignment of `T`.
[759](https://docs.rs#759)///
[760](https://docs.rs#760)/// Because of this, only one [`CopyRecord`] is returned specifying the record of the
[761](https://docs.rs#761)/// entire block of copied data. If the `src` iterator is empty, returns `None`.
[762](https://docs.rs#762)pub fn copy_from_iter_to_offset_with_align_packed<T: Copy, Iter: Iterator<Item = T>, S: Slab>(
[763](https://docs.rs#763)    mut src: Iter,
[764](https://docs.rs#764)    dst: &mut S,
[765](https://docs.rs#765)    start_offset: usize,
[766](https://docs.rs#766)    min_alignment: usize,
[767](https://docs.rs#767)) -> Result<Option<CopyRecord>, CopyError> {
[768](https://docs.rs#768)    let first_record = if let Some(first_item) = src.next() {
[769](https://docs.rs#769)        copy_to_offset_with_align(&first_item, dst, start_offset, min_alignment)?
[770](https://docs.rs#770)    } else {
[771](https://docs.rs#771)        return Ok(None);
[772](https://docs.rs#772)    };
[773](https://docs.rs#773)
[774](https://docs.rs#774)    let mut prev_record = first_record;
[775](https://docs.rs#775)
[776](https://docs.rs#776)    for item in src {
[777](https://docs.rs#777)        let copy_record = copy_to_offset_with_align(&item, dst, prev_record.copy_end_offset, 1)?;
[778](https://docs.rs#778)        prev_record = copy_record;
[779](https://docs.rs#779)    }
[780](https://docs.rs#780)
[781](https://docs.rs#781)    Ok(Some(CopyRecord {
[782](https://docs.rs#782)        copy_start_offset: first_record.copy_start_offset,
[783](https://docs.rs#783)        copy_end_offset: prev_record.copy_end_offset,
[784](https://docs.rs#784)        copy_end_offset_padded: prev_record.copy_end_offset_padded,
[785](https://docs.rs#785)    }))

}## Expand description

Represents a contiguous piece of a single allocation with some layout that is used as a data copying destination. May be wholly or partially uninitialized.

This trait is *basically* equivalent to implementing `Deref`/`DerefMut` with
`Target = [MaybeUninit<u8>]` in terms of safety requirements. It is a separate
trait for the extra flexibility having a trait we own provides: namely, the ability
to implement it on foreign types.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

Implementors of this trait must ensure these guarantees:

- The memory range represented by `base_ptr`and`size`**may**be wholly or partially uninitialized
- `base_ptr`- **must**point to a valid, single allocation of at least- `size`bytes.
- `size`- **must not**be greater than- `isize::MAX`

Assume the lifetime of a shared borrow of self is named `'a`:

- `base_ptr`- **must**be- [valid](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ptr/index.html#safety)for- `'a`
- `base_ptr`- **must**be mutably aliased for- *not*- `'a`- It is necessary but not sufficient for this requirement that
**no outside**may exist to its data, even if they are unused by user code.*mutable*references

- It is necessary but not sufficient for this requirement that

Assume the lifetime of a mutable borrow of self is named `'a`:

- `base_ptr_mut`- **must**be- [valid](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ptr/index.html#safety)for- `'a`
- `base_ptr_mut`- **must**be aliased at all for- *not*- `'a`- It is necessary but not sufficient for this requirement that
**no outside references**may exist to its data, even if they are unused by user code.

- It is necessary but not sufficient for this requirement that

Also see the [crate-level safety documentation](https://docs.rs/index.html#safety).

Interpret a range of `self` as a byte slice. This assumes that **all bytes**
within `range` are initialized.

In the future, this will hopefully not be needed as this operation will be equivalent to
something like `self.as_maybe_uninit_bytes_mut()[range].assume_init()`, but the `core`/`std`
implementation for this is still being scaffolded.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-3)Safety

Assuming that the safety guarantees for creating `self` were followed,
the only extra requirement for this to be safe is that **all memory**
within `range` must be **initialized**. If *any bytes* within
this range are not initialized, using this function is *instantly  undefined
behavior*, even if you

*do noting*with the result.

Also see the [crate-level Safety documentation](https://docs.rs/index.html#safety) for more.

# copy_to_offset_with_align in presser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/presser/latest/target-redirect/i686-unknown-linux-gnu/presser/fn.copy_to_offset_with_align.html

`pub fn copy_to_offset_with_align<T: `[Copy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Copy.html), S: [Slab](https://docs.rs/trait.Slab.html)>(
    src: [&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html),
    dst: [&mut S](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html),
    start_offset: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    min_alignment: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[CopyRecord](https://docs.rs/struct.CopyRecord.html), [CopyError](https://docs.rs/enum.CopyError.html)>## Expand description

Copies `src` into the memory represented by `dst` starting at a minimum location
of `start_offset` bytes past the start of `dst` and with minimum alignment
`min_alignment`.

- `start_offset`is the offset into the allocation represented by- `dst`, in bytes, before which any copied data will- *certainly not*be placed. However, the actual beginning of the copied data may not be exactly at- `start_offset`if padding bytes are needed to satisfy alignment requirements. The actual beginning of the copied bytes is contained in the returned- `CopyRecord`
- `min_alignment`is the minimum alignment to which the copy will be aligned. The copy may not actually be aligned to- `min_alignment`depending on the alignment requirements of- `T`.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

This function is safe on its own, however it is very possible to do unsafe
things if you read the copied data in the wrong way. See the
[crate-level Safety documentation](https://docs.rs/index.html#safety) for more.

---

`copy_start_offset: `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)The offset from the start of the allocation, in bytes, at which the copy operation began to write data.

Not necessarily equal to the `start_offset`, since this offset
includes necessary padding to assure alignment.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.copy_end_offset)

This does not include any padding at the end necessary to maintain alignment requirements.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.copy_end_offset_padded)

`copy_end_offset_padded: `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)The offset from the start of the allocation, in bytes, at which the copy operation no longer wrote data, plus any padding necessary to maintain derived alignment requirements.

# clone_into_maybe_uninit_slice in presser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/presser/latest/target-redirect/i686-unknown-linux-gnu/presser/fn.clone_into_maybe_uninit_slice.html

```
pub fn clone_into_maybe_uninit_slice<'a, T>(
    src: &
```
[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html),
    dst: &'a mut [[MaybeUninit](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/maybe_uninit/union.MaybeUninit.html)<T>],
) -> &'a mut [[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html)## Expand description

Clones the elements from `src` to `dst`, returning a mutable reference to the now initialized contents of `dst`.
Any already initialized elements will not be dropped.

If `T` implements `Copy`, use `copy_into_maybe_uninit_slice`

This is similar to [ slice::clone_from_slice](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.clone_from_slice) but does not drop existing elements. This is identical to the implementation of
the method

`write_to_slice_cloned` on [, but that API is as yet unstable.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/maybe_uninit/union.MaybeUninit.html)

`MaybeUninit`[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

This function will panic if the two slices have different lengths, or if the implementation of `Clone` panics.

If there is a panic, the already cloned elements will be dropped.

# copy_from_iter_to_offset_with_align_packed in presser - Rust

of `start_offset` bytes past the start of `self`.

- `start_offset`is the offset into the allocation represented by- `dst`, in bytes, before which any copied data will- *certainly not*be placed. [§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

You promise that the given `Vec` already has at least `length` capacity. You also promise to either fill all items before dropping
the returned slice, or to continue to not violate validity rules for any items that you do not initialize.

# presser - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/presser/0.3.1/x86_64-apple-darwin/presser/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#-presser)`🗜 presser`

**Utilities to help make copying data around into raw, possibly-uninitialized buffers
easier and safer.**

[§](https://docs.rs#motivation)Motivation

`presser` can help you when copying data into raw buffers. One primary use-case is copying data into
graphics-api-allocated buffers which will then be accessed by the GPU. Common methods for doing this
right now in Rust can often invoke UB in subtle and hard-to-see ways. For example, viewing an allocated
but uninitialized buffer as an `&mut [u8]` **is instantly undefined behavior***, and `transmute`ing even a
`T: Copy` type which has *any padding bytes in its layout* as a `&[u8]` to be the source of a copy is
**also instantly undefined behavior**, in both cases because it is *invalid* to create a reference to an invalid
value (and uninitialized memory is an invalid `u8`), *even if* your code never actually accesses that memory.
This immediately makes what seems like the most straightforward way to copy data into buffers unsound 😬.

`presser` helps with this by allowing you to view raw allocated memory of some size as a “[ Slab](https://docs.rs/trait.Slab.html)” of memory and then
provides

*safe, valid*ways to copy data into that memory. For example, you could implement

[for your GPU-allocated buffer type, or use the built-in](https://docs.rs/trait.Slab.html)

`Slab`[workflow described below, then use](https://docs.rs/struct.RawAllocation.html)

`RawAllocation`[to copy any](https://docs.rs/fn.copy_to_offset_with_align.html)

`copy_to_offset_with_align``T: Copy` data into that buffer safely for use on the GPU.
Of course, if your `T` doesn’t have the correct layout the GPU expects, accessing it on the GPU side may still be
unsound or at least give an error.* *If you’re currently thinking to yourself “bah! what’s the issue? surely an uninit u8 is just any random bit pattern
and that’s fine we don’t care,”  check out this blog post by
@RalfJung, one of the people leading the effort to better define Rust’s memory and execution model. As is explored
in that blog post, an  uninit piece of memory is not simply an arbitrary bit pattern, it is a wholly separate
state about a piece of memory, outside of its value, which lets the compiler perform optimizations that reorder,
delete, and otherwise change the actual execution flow of your program in ways that cannot be described simply
by “the value could have some possible bit pattern”. LLVM and Clang are changing themselves to require special
*

`noundef` attribute to perform many important optimizations that are otherwise unsound. For a concrete example
of the sorts of problems this can cause,
see this issue @scottmcm hit.[§](https://docs.rs#introduction)Introduction

The main idea is to implement [ Slab](https://docs.rs/trait.Slab.html) on raw-buffer-esque-types (see

[the](https://docs.rs/trait.Slab.html#Safety)), which then enables the use of the other functions within the crate.

`Slab` safety docsDepending on your use case, you may be able to implement [ Slab](https://docs.rs/trait.Slab.html) directly for your buffer type, or it may
be more convenient or necessary to create a wrapping struct that borrows your raw buffer type and in turn
implements

[. For an example of this, see](https://docs.rs/trait.Slab.html)

`Slab`[and](https://docs.rs/struct.RawAllocation.html)

`RawAllocation`[, which you may also use directly. The idea is to create a](https://docs.rs/struct.BorrowedRawAllocation.html)

`BorrowedRawAllocation`[to your buffer, which you then borrow into a](https://docs.rs/struct.RawAllocation.html)

`RawAllocation`[(which implements](https://docs.rs/struct.BorrowedRawAllocation.html)

`BorrowedRawAllocation`[) by calling the unsafe function](https://docs.rs/trait.Slab.html)

`Slab`

`RawAllocation::borrow_as_slab`Once you have a slab, you can use the copy helper functions provided at the crate root, for example,
[ copy_to_offset](https://docs.rs/fn.copy_to_offset.html) and

[.](https://docs.rs/fn.copy_to_offset_with_align.html)

`copy_to_offset_with_align`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(C)]
struct MyDataStruct {
    a: u8,
    b: u32,
}
let my_data = MyDataStruct { a: 0, b: 42 };
// allocate an uninit buffer of some size
let my_buffer: MyBufferType = some_api.alloc_buffer_size(2048);
// use `RawAllocation` helper to allow access to a presser `Slab`.
// alternatively, you could implement the `Slab` on `MyByfferType` directly if that
// type is owned by your code!
let raw_allocation = presser::RawAllocation::from_raw_parts(my_buffer.ptr(), my_buffer.size());
// here we assert that we have exclusive access to the data in the buffer, and get the actual
// `Slab` to use to copy into.
let slab = unsafe { raw_allocation.borrow_as_slab(); }
// now we may safely copy `my_data` into `my_buffer`, starting at a minimum offset of 0 into the buffer
let copy_record = presser::copy_to_offset(&my_data, &mut slab, 0)?;
// note that due to alignment requirements of `my_data`, the *actual* start of the bytes of
// `my_data` may be placed at a different offset than requested. so, we check the returned
// `CopyRecord` to check the actual start offset of the copied data.
let actual_start_offset = copy_record.copy_start_offset;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#no_std)`#[no_std]`

This crate supports `no_std` environments by building without the ‘`std`’ feature. This will limit some
of the fuctions the crate can perform.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

An important note is that obeying the safety rules specified in the [ Slab](https://docs.rs/trait.Slab.html) safety documentation

*only*guarantees safety for the

*direct results*of the copy operations performed by the helper functions exported at the crate root (and the safe functions on

[).](https://docs.rs/trait.Slab.html)

`Slab`**However**, it is

*guaranteed that operations which would previously have been safe to perform using same backing memory that the*

**not**[you copied into used are still safe.](https://docs.rs/trait.Slab.html)

`Slab`For example, say you have a fully-initialized
chunk of bytes (like a `Vec<u8>`), which you view as a [ Slab](https://docs.rs/trait.Slab.html), and then (safely) perform a copy
operation into using

[. If the](https://docs.rs/fn.copy_to_offset.html)

`copy_to_offset``T` you copied into it has any padding bytes in
its memory layout, then the memory locations where those padding bytes now exist in the underlying `Vec`’s
memory must now be treated as uninitialized. As such, taking any view into that byte vector which
relies on those newly-uninit bytes being initialized to be valid (for example, taking a `&[u8]` slice of the `Vec`
which includes those bytes, *) is now instant*

**even if your code never actually reads from that slice****undefined behavior**.

# lib.rs - source

# presser/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! # `🗜 presser`
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! **Utilities to help make copying data around into raw, possibly-uninitialized buffers
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! easier and safer.**
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//!
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! ## Motivation
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//!
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! `presser` can help you when copying data into raw buffers. One primary use-case is copying data into
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! graphics-api-allocated buffers which will then be accessed by the GPU. Common methods for doing this
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! right now in Rust can often invoke UB in subtle and hard-to-see ways. For example, viewing an allocated
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! but uninitialized buffer as an `&mut [u8]` **is instantly undefined behavior**\*, and `transmute`ing even a
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! `T: Copy` type which has *any padding bytes in its layout* as a `&[u8]` to be the source of a copy is
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! **also instantly undefined behavior**, in both cases because it is *invalid* to create a reference to an invalid
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! value (and uninitialized memory is an invalid `u8`), *even if* your code never actually accesses that memory.
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! This immediately makes what seems like the most straightforward way to copy data into buffers unsound 😬.
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//!
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! `presser` helps with this by allowing you to view raw allocated memory of some size as a "[`Slab`]" of memory and then
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! provides *safe, valid* ways to copy data into that memory. For example, you could implement [`Slab`] for your
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! GPU-allocated buffer type, or use the built-in [`RawAllocation`] workflow described below, then use
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! [`copy_to_offset_with_align`] to copy any `T: Copy` data into that buffer safely for use on the GPU.
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! Of course, if your `T` doesn't have the correct layout the GPU expects, accessing it on the GPU side may still be
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! unsound or at least give an error.
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! \* *If you're currently thinking to yourself "bah! what's the issue? surely an uninit u8 is just any random bit pattern
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! and that's fine we don't care," [check out this blog post](https://www.ralfj.de/blog/2019/07/14/uninit.html) by
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! @RalfJung, one of the people leading the effort to better define Rust's memory and execution model. As is explored
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! in that blog post, an *uninit* piece of memory is not simply *an arbitrary bit pattern*, it is a wholly separate
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! state about a piece of memory, outside of its value, which lets the compiler perform optimizations that reorder,
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! delete, and otherwise change the actual execution flow of your program in ways that cannot be described simply
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! by "the value could have *some* possible bit pattern". LLVM and Clang are changing themselves to require special
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! `noundef` attribute to perform many important optimizations that are otherwise unsound. For a concrete example
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! of the sorts of problems this can cause,
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! [see this issue @scottmcm hit](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/98919#issuecomment-1186106387).*
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//!
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! ## Introduction
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! The main idea is to implement [`Slab`] on raw-buffer-esque-types (see [the `Slab` safety docs][Slab#Safety]),
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! which then enables the use of the other functions within the crate.
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//!
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! Depending on your use case, you may be able to implement [`Slab`] directly for your buffer type, or it may
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! be more convenient or necessary to create a wrapping struct that borrows your raw buffer type and in turn
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! implements [`Slab`]. For an example of this, see [`RawAllocation`] and [`BorrowedRawAllocation`], which you
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! may also use directly. The idea is to create a [`RawAllocation`] to your buffer, which you then borrow into
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! a [`BorrowedRawAllocation`] (which implements [`Slab`]) by calling the unsafe function
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! [`RawAllocation::borrow_as_slab`]
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! Once you have a slab, you can use the copy helper functions provided at the crate root, for example,
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! [`copy_to_offset`] and [`copy_to_offset_with_align`].
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//!
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! ### Example
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//!
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! ```rust,ignore
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//! #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! #[repr(C)]
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//! struct MyDataStruct {
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//!     a: u8,
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!     b: u32,
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! }
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//!
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//! let my_data = MyDataStruct { a: 0, b: 42 };
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//!
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! // allocate an uninit buffer of some size
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//! let my_buffer: MyBufferType = some_api.alloc_buffer_size(2048);
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//!
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//! // use `RawAllocation` helper to allow access to a presser `Slab`.
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! // alternatively, you could implement the `Slab` on `MyByfferType` directly if that
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! // type is owned by your code!
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//! let raw_allocation = presser::RawAllocation::from_raw_parts(my_buffer.ptr(), my_buffer.size());
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//!
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! // here we assert that we have exclusive access to the data in the buffer, and get the actual
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//! // `Slab` to use to copy into.
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//! let slab = unsafe { raw_allocation.borrow_as_slab(); }
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//!
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//! // now we may safely copy `my_data` into `my_buffer`, starting at a minimum offset of 0 into the buffer
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//! let copy_record = presser::copy_to_offset(&my_data, &mut slab, 0)?;
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//!
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//! // note that due to alignment requirements of `my_data`, the *actual* start of the bytes of
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! // `my_data` may be placed at a different offset than requested. so, we check the returned
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! // `CopyRecord` to check the actual start offset of the copied data.
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! let actual_start_offset = copy_record.copy_start_offset;
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//! ```
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//!
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! ### `#[no_std]`
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//!
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//! This crate supports `no_std` environments by building without the '`std`' feature. This will limit some
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! of the fuctions the crate can perform.
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//!
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! # Safety
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//!
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//! An important note is that obeying the safety rules specified in the [`Slab`] safety documentation
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//! *only* guarantees safety for the *direct results* of the copy operations performed by the
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//! helper functions exported at the crate root (and the safe functions on [`Slab`]). **However**,
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//! it is ***not*** guaranteed that operations which would previously have been safe to perform
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//! using same backing memory that the [`Slab`] you copied into used are still safe.
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//!
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//! For example, say you have a fully-initialized
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//! chunk of bytes (like a `Vec<u8>`), which you view as a [`Slab`], and then (safely) perform a copy
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//! operation into using [`copy_to_offset`]. If the `T` you copied into it has any padding bytes in
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//! its memory layout, then the memory locations where those padding bytes now exist in the underlying `Vec`'s
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//! memory must now be treated as uninitialized. As such, taking any view into that byte vector which
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//! relies on those newly-uninit bytes being initialized to be valid (for example, taking a `&[u8]` slice of the `Vec`
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//! which includes those bytes, ***even if your code never actually reads from that slice***)
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//! is now instant **undefined behavior**.
[104](https://docs.rs#104)#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "std"), no_std)]
[105](https://docs.rs#105)#![deny(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]

[111](https://docs.rs#111)// .github/workflows/rustdoc-pages.yml workflow)

[120](https://docs.rs#120)/// Represents a contiguous piece of a single allocation with some layout that is used as a
[121](https://docs.rs#121)/// data copying destination. May be wholly or partially uninitialized.
[122](https://docs.rs#122)///
[123](https://docs.rs#123)/// This trait is *basically* equivalent to implementing `Deref`/`DerefMut` with
[124](https://docs.rs#124)/// `Target = [MaybeUninit<u8>]` in terms of safety requirements. It is a separate
[125](https://docs.rs#125)/// trait for the extra flexibility having a trait we own provides: namely, the ability
[126](https://docs.rs#126)/// to implement it on foreign types.
[127](https://docs.rs#127)///
[128](https://docs.rs#128)/// # Safety
[129](https://docs.rs#129)///
[130](https://docs.rs#130)/// Implementors of this trait must ensure these guarantees:
[131](https://docs.rs#131)///
[132](https://docs.rs#132)/// - The memory range represented by `base_ptr` and `size` **may** be wholly or partially uninitialized
[133](https://docs.rs#133)/// - `base_ptr` **must** point to a valid, single allocation of at least `size` bytes.
[134](https://docs.rs#134)/// - `size` **must not** be greater than `isize::MAX`
[135](https://docs.rs#135)///
[136](https://docs.rs#136)/// Assume the lifetime of a shared borrow of self is named `'a`:
[137](https://docs.rs#137)///
[138](https://docs.rs#138)/// - `base_ptr` **must** be [valid][`core::ptr#safety`] for `'a`
[139](https://docs.rs#139)/// - `base_ptr` **must *not*** be mutably aliased for `'a`
[140](https://docs.rs#140)///     - It is necessary but not sufficient for this requirement that
[141](https://docs.rs#141)/// **no outside *mutable* references** may exist to its data, even if they are unused by user code.
[142](https://docs.rs#142)///
[143](https://docs.rs#143)/// Assume the lifetime of a mutable borrow of self is named `'a`:
[144](https://docs.rs#144)///
[145](https://docs.rs#145)/// - `base_ptr_mut` **must** be [valid][`core::ptr#safety`] for `'a`
[146](https://docs.rs#146)/// - `base_ptr_mut` **must *not*** be aliased at all for `'a`
[147](https://docs.rs#147)///     - It is necessary but not sufficient for this requirement that
[148](https://docs.rs#148)/// **no outside references** may exist to its data, even if they are unused by user code.
[149](https://docs.rs#149)///
[150](https://docs.rs#150)/// Also see the [crate-level safety documentation][`crate#safety`].
[151](https://docs.rs#151)pub unsafe trait Slab {
[152](https://docs.rs#152)    /// Get a pointer to the beginning of the allocation represented by `self`.
[153](https://docs.rs#153)    fn base_ptr(&self) -> *const u8;
[154](https://docs.rs#154)
[155](https://docs.rs#155)    /// Get a pointer to the beginning of the allocation represented by `self`.
[156](https://docs.rs#156)    fn base_ptr_mut(&mut self) -> *mut u8;
[157](https://docs.rs#157)
[158](https://docs.rs#158)    /// Get the size of the allocation represented by `self`.
[159](https://docs.rs#159)    fn size(&self) -> usize;
[160](https://docs.rs#160)
[161](https://docs.rs#161)    /// Interpret a portion of `self` as a slice of [`MaybeUninit<u8>`]. This is likely not
[162](https://docs.rs#162)    /// incredibly useful, you probably want to use [`Slab::as_maybe_uninit_bytes_mut`]
[163](https://docs.rs#163)    fn as_maybe_uninit_bytes(&self) -> &[MaybeUninit<u8>] {
[164](https://docs.rs#164)        // SAFETY: Safe so long as top level safety guarantees are held, since
[165](https://docs.rs#165)        // `MaybeUninit` has same layout as bare type.
[166](https://docs.rs#166)        unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(self.base_ptr().cast(), self.size()) }
[167](https://docs.rs#167)    }
[168](https://docs.rs#168)
[169](https://docs.rs#169)    /// Interpret a portion of `self` as a mutable slice of [`MaybeUninit<u8>`].
[170](https://docs.rs#170)    fn as_maybe_uninit_bytes_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [MaybeUninit<u8>] {
[171](https://docs.rs#171)        // SAFETY: Safe so long as top level safety guarantees are held, since
[172](https://docs.rs#172)        // `MaybeUninit` has same layout as bare type.
[173](https://docs.rs#173)        unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(self.base_ptr_mut().cast(), self.size()) }
[174](https://docs.rs#174)    }
[175](https://docs.rs#175)
[176](https://docs.rs#176)    /// Interpret `self` as a byte slice. This assumes that **all bytes**
[177](https://docs.rs#177)    /// in `self` are initialized.
[178](https://docs.rs#178)    ///
[179](https://docs.rs#179)    /// # Safety
[180](https://docs.rs#180)    ///
[181](https://docs.rs#181)    /// Assuming that the safety guarantees for creating `self` were followed,
[182](https://docs.rs#182)    /// the only extra requirement for this to be safe is that **all memory**
[183](https://docs.rs#183)    /// within the range of `self` must be **initialized**. If *any bytes* within
[184](https://docs.rs#184)    /// this range are not initialized, using this function is *instantly **undefined
[185](https://docs.rs#185)    /// behavior***, even if you *do noting* with the result.
[186](https://docs.rs#186)    ///
[187](https://docs.rs#187)    /// Also see the [crate-level Safety documentation][`crate#safety`] for more.
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    unsafe fn assume_initialized_as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
[189](https://docs.rs#189)        // SAFETY: same requirements as function-level safety assuming the requirements
[190](https://docs.rs#190)        // for creating `self` are met
[191](https://docs.rs#191)        unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(self.base_ptr().cast(), self.size()) }
[192](https://docs.rs#192)    }
[193](https://docs.rs#193)
[194](https://docs.rs#194)    /// Interpret `self` as a mutable byte slice. This assumes that **all bytes**
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    /// in `self` are initialized.
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    ///
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    /// # Safety
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    ///
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    /// Assuming that the safety guarantees for creating `self` were followed,
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    /// the only extra requirement for this to be safe is that **all memory**
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    /// within the range of `self` must be **initialized**. If *any bytes* within
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    /// this range are not initialized, using this function is *instantly **undefined
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    /// behavior***, even if you *do noting* with the result.
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    ///
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    /// Also see the [crate-level Safety documentation][`crate#safety`] for more.
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    unsafe fn assume_initialized_as_bytes_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [u8] {
[207](https://docs.rs#207)        // SAFETY: same requirements as function-level safety assuming the requirements
[208](https://docs.rs#208)        // for creating `self` are met
[209](https://docs.rs#209)        unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(self.base_ptr_mut().cast(), self.size()) }
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    }
[211](https://docs.rs#211)
[212](https://docs.rs#212)    /// Interpret a range of `self` as a byte slice. This assumes that **all bytes**
[213](https://docs.rs#213)    /// within `range` are initialized.
[214](https://docs.rs#214)    ///
[215](https://docs.rs#215)    /// In the future, this will hopefully not be needed as this operation will be equivalent to
[216](https://docs.rs#216)    /// something like `self.as_maybe_uninit_bytes_mut()[range].assume_init()`, but the `core`/`std`
[217](https://docs.rs#217)    /// implementation for this is still being scaffolded.
[218](https://docs.rs#218)    ///
[219](https://docs.rs#219)    /// # Safety
[220](https://docs.rs#220)    ///
[221](https://docs.rs#221)    /// Assuming that the safety guarantees for creating `self` were followed,
[222](https://docs.rs#222)    /// the only extra requirement for this to be safe is that **all memory**
[223](https://docs.rs#223)    /// within `range` must be **initialized**. If *any bytes* within
[224](https://docs.rs#224)    /// this range are not initialized, using this function is *instantly **undefined
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    /// behavior***, even if you *do noting* with the result.
[226](https://docs.rs#226)    ///
[227](https://docs.rs#227)    /// Also see the [crate-level Safety documentation][`crate#safety`] for more.
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    unsafe fn assume_range_initialized_as_bytes<R>(&self, range: R) -> &[u8]
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    where
[230](https://docs.rs#230)        R: core::slice::SliceIndex<[MaybeUninit<u8>], Output = [MaybeUninit<u8>]>,
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    {
[232](https://docs.rs#232)        let maybe_uninit_slice = &self.as_maybe_uninit_bytes()[range];
[233](https://docs.rs#233)        // SAFETY: same requirements as function-level safety assuming the requirements
[234](https://docs.rs#234)        // for creating `self` are met since `MaybeUnint<T>` has same layout as `T`
[235](https://docs.rs#235)        unsafe {
[236](https://docs.rs#236)            core::slice::from_raw_parts(
[237](https://docs.rs#237)                maybe_uninit_slice.as_ptr().cast(),
[238](https://docs.rs#238)                maybe_uninit_slice.len(),
[239](https://docs.rs#239)            )
[240](https://docs.rs#240)        }
[241](https://docs.rs#241)    }
[242](https://docs.rs#242)
[243](https://docs.rs#243)    /// Interpret a range of `self` as a mutable byte slice. This assumes that **all bytes**
[244](https://docs.rs#244)    /// within `range` are initialized.
[245](https://docs.rs#245)    ///
[246](https://docs.rs#246)    /// In the future, this will hopefully not be needed as this operation will be equivalent to
[247](https://docs.rs#247)    /// something like `self.as_maybe_uninit_bytes_mut()[range].assume_init()`, but the `core`/`std`
[248](https://docs.rs#248)    /// implementation for this is still being scaffolded.
[249](https://docs.rs#249)    ///
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    /// # Safety
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    ///
[252](https://docs.rs#252)    /// Assuming that the safety guarantees for creating `self` were followed,
[253](https://docs.rs#253)    /// the only extra requirement for this to be safe is that **all memory**
[254](https://docs.rs#254)    /// within `range` must be **initialized**. If *any bytes* within
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    /// this range are not initialized, using this function is *instantly **undefined
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    /// behavior***, even if you *do noting* with the result.
[257](https://docs.rs#257)    ///
[258](https://docs.rs#258)    /// Also see the [crate-level Safety documentation][`crate#safety`] for more.
[259](https://docs.rs#259)    unsafe fn assume_range_initialized_as_bytes_mut<R>(&mut self, range: R) -> &mut [u8]
[260](https://docs.rs#260)    where
[261](https://docs.rs#261)        R: core::slice::SliceIndex<[MaybeUninit<u8>], Output = [MaybeUninit<u8>]>,
[262](https://docs.rs#262)    {
[263](https://docs.rs#263)        let maybe_uninit_slice = &mut self.as_maybe_uninit_bytes_mut()[range];
[264](https://docs.rs#264)        // SAFETY: same requirements as function-level safety assuming the requirements
[265](https://docs.rs#265)        // for creating `self` are met since `MaybeUnint<T>` has same layout as `T`
[266](https://docs.rs#266)        unsafe {
[267](https://docs.rs#267)            core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(
[268](https://docs.rs#268)                maybe_uninit_slice.as_mut_ptr().cast(),
[269](https://docs.rs#269)                maybe_uninit_slice.len(),
[270](https://docs.rs#270)            )
[271](https://docs.rs#271)        }
[272](https://docs.rs#272)    }
[273](https://docs.rs#273)}
[274](https://docs.rs#274)
[275](https://docs.rs#275)// SAFETY: The captured `[MaybeUninit<u8>]` will all be part of the same allocation object, and borrowck
[276](https://docs.rs#276)// will assure that the borrows that occur on `self` on the relevant methods live long enough since they are
[277](https://docs.rs#277)// native borrows anyway.
[278](https://docs.rs#278)unsafe impl Slab for [MaybeUninit<u8>] {
[279](https://docs.rs#279)    fn base_ptr(&self) -> *const u8 {
[280](https://docs.rs#280)        self.as_ptr().cast()
[281](https://docs.rs#281)    }
[282](https://docs.rs#282)
[283](https://docs.rs#283)    fn base_ptr_mut(&mut self) -> *mut u8 {
[284](https://docs.rs#284)        self.as_mut_ptr().cast()
[285](https://docs.rs#285)    }
[286](https://docs.rs#286)
[287](https://docs.rs#287)    fn size(&self) -> usize {
[288](https://docs.rs#288)        core::mem::size_of_val(self)
[289](https://docs.rs#289)    }
[290](https://docs.rs#290)}
[291](https://docs.rs#291)
[292](https://docs.rs#292)/// Takes a `Vec` and unsafely resizes it to the given length, returning a mutable slice to `MaybeUninit<T>` for each
[293](https://docs.rs#293)/// item in the newly-resized `Vec`.
[294](https://docs.rs#294)///
[295](https://docs.rs#295)/// # Safety
[296](https://docs.rs#296)///
[297](https://docs.rs#297)/// You promise that the given `Vec` already has at least `length` capacity. You also promise to either fill all items before dropping
[298](https://docs.rs#298)/// the returned slice, or to continue to not violate validity rules for any items that you do not initialize.
[299](https://docs.rs#299)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[300](https://docs.rs#300)pub unsafe fn maybe_uninit_slice_from_vec<T>(
[301](https://docs.rs#301)    vec: &mut Vec<T>,
[302](https://docs.rs#302)    length: usize,
[303](https://docs.rs#303)) -> &mut [MaybeUninit<T>] {
[304](https://docs.rs#304)    // SAFETY: As long as the function-level safety rules are met, this is valid
[305](https://docs.rs#305)    unsafe {
[306](https://docs.rs#306)        #[allow(clippy::uninit_vec)]
[307](https://docs.rs#307)        vec.set_len(length);
[308](https://docs.rs#308)    }
[309](https://docs.rs#309)
[310](https://docs.rs#310)    // SAFETY: If function-level safety is met, then we are constructing a slice within a single allocation. `MaybeUninit<T>` is valid
[311](https://docs.rs#311)    // even for uninit memory, and has the same memory layout as `T`.
[312](https://docs.rs#312)    unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(vec.as_mut_ptr().cast::<MaybeUninit<T>>(), length) }

[315](https://docs.rs#315)/// Copies the elements from `src` to `dst`, returning a mutable reference to the now initialized contents of `dst`.

[317](https://docs.rs#317)/// If `T` does not implement `Copy`, use [`clone_into_maybe_uninit_slice`]
[318](https://docs.rs#318)///
[319](https://docs.rs#319)/// This is similar to [`slice::copy_from_slice`]. This is identical to the implementation of the method
[320](https://docs.rs#320)/// `write_to_slice` on [`MaybeUninit`], but that API is as yet unstable.
[321](https://docs.rs#321)///
[322](https://docs.rs#322)/// # Panics
[323](https://docs.rs#323)///
[324](https://docs.rs#324)/// This function will panic if the two slices have different lengths.
[325](https://docs.rs#325)pub fn copy_into_maybe_uninit_slice<'a, T>(src: &[T], dst: &'a mut [MaybeUninit<T>]) -> &'a mut [T]
[326](https://docs.rs#326)where
[327](https://docs.rs#327)    T: Copy,
[328](https://docs.rs#328){
[329](https://docs.rs#329)    let uninit_src: &[MaybeUninit<T>] =
[330](https://docs.rs#330)        // SAFETY: &[T] and &[MaybeUninit<T>] have the same layout

[339](https://docs.rs#339)/// Clones the elements from `src` to `dst`, returning a mutable reference to the now initialized contents of `dst`.
[340](https://docs.rs#340)/// Any already initialized elements will not be dropped.
[341](https://docs.rs#341)///
[342](https://docs.rs#342)/// If `T` implements `Copy`, use [`copy_into_maybe_uninit_slice`]
[343](https://docs.rs#343)///
[344](https://docs.rs#344)/// This is similar to [`slice::clone_from_slice`] but does not drop existing elements. This is identical to the implementation of
[345](https://docs.rs#345)/// the method `write_to_slice_cloned` on [`MaybeUninit`], but that API is as yet unstable.
[346](https://docs.rs#346)///
[347](https://docs.rs#347)/// # Panics
[348](https://docs.rs#348)///
[349](https://docs.rs#349)/// This function will panic if the two slices have different lengths, or if the implementation of `Clone` panics.
[350](https://docs.rs#350)///
[351](https://docs.rs#351)/// If there is a panic, the already cloned elements will be dropped.
[352](https://docs.rs#352)pub fn clone_into_maybe_uninit_slice<'a, T>(src: &[T], dst: &'a mut [MaybeUninit<T>]) -> &'a mut [T]
[353](https://docs.rs#353)where
[354](https://docs.rs#354)    T: Clone,
[355](https://docs.rs#355){
[356](https://docs.rs#356)    // unlike copy_from_slice this does not call clone_from_slice on the slice
[357](https://docs.rs#357)    // this is because `MaybeUninit<T: Clone>` does not implement Clone.
[358](https://docs.rs#358)
[359](https://docs.rs#359)    struct Guard<'a, T> {
[360](https://docs.rs#360)        slice: &'a mut [MaybeUninit<T>],
[361](https://docs.rs#361)        initialized: usize,
[362](https://docs.rs#362)    }
[363](https://docs.rs#363)
[364](https://docs.rs#364)    impl<'a, T> Drop for Guard<'a, T> {
[365](https://docs.rs#365)        fn drop(&mut self) {
[366](https://docs.rs#366)            let initialized_part = &mut self.slice[..self.initialized];
[367](https://docs.rs#367)            // SAFETY: this raw slice will contain only initialized objects
[368](https://docs.rs#368)            // that's why, it is allowed to drop it.
[369](https://docs.rs#369)            unsafe {
[370](https://docs.rs#370)                core::ptr::drop_in_place(
[371](https://docs.rs#371)                    &mut *(initialized_part as *mut [MaybeUninit<T>] as *mut [T]),
[372](https://docs.rs#372)                );
[373](https://docs.rs#373)            }
[374](https://docs.rs#374)        }
[375](https://docs.rs#375)    }
[376](https://docs.rs#376)
[377](https://docs.rs#377)    assert_eq!(
[378](https://docs.rs#378)        dst.len(),
[379](https://docs.rs#379)        src.len(),
[380](https://docs.rs#380)        "destination and source slices have different lengths"
[381](https://docs.rs#381)    );
[382](https://docs.rs#382)    // NOTE: We need to explicitly slice them to the same length
[383](https://docs.rs#383)    // for bounds checking to be elided, and the optimizer will
[384](https://docs.rs#384)    // generate memcpy for simple cases (for example T = u8).
[385](https://docs.rs#385)    let len = dst.len();
[386](https://docs.rs#386)    let src = &src[..len];
[387](https://docs.rs#387)
[388](https://docs.rs#388)    // guard is needed b/c panic might happen during a clone
[389](https://docs.rs#389)    let mut guard = Guard {
[390](https://docs.rs#390)        slice: dst,
[391](https://docs.rs#391)        initialized: 0,
[392](https://docs.rs#392)    };
[393](https://docs.rs#393)
[394](https://docs.rs#394)    #[allow(clippy::needless_range_loop)]
[395](https://docs.rs#395)    for i in 0..len {
[396](https://docs.rs#396)        guard.slice[i].write(src[i].clone());
[397](https://docs.rs#397)        guard.initialized += 1;
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    }
[399](https://docs.rs#399)
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    #[allow(clippy::mem_forget)]
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    core::mem::forget(guard);
[402](https://docs.rs#402)
[403](https://docs.rs#403)    // SAFETY: Valid elements have just been written into `this` so it is initialized
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    unsafe { &mut *(dst as *mut [MaybeUninit<T>] as *mut [T]) }
[405](https://docs.rs#405)}

[464](https://docs.rs#464)unsafe impl<'a> Slab for BorrowedRawAllocation<'a> {

[477](https://docs.rs#477)
[478](https://docs.rs#478)/// Given pointer and offset, returns a new offset aligned to `align`.
[479](https://docs.rs#479)///
[480](https://docs.rs#480)/// `align` *must* be a power of two and >= 1 or else the result is meaningless.
[481](https://docs.rs#481)fn align_offset_up_to(ptr: usize, offset: usize, align: usize) -> Option<usize> {
[482](https://docs.rs#482)    let offsetted_ptr = ptr.checked_add(offset)?;
[483](https://docs.rs#483)    let aligned_ptr = offsetted_ptr.checked_add(align - 1)? & !(align - 1);
[484](https://docs.rs#484)    // don't need to check since we know aligned_ptr is >= ptr at this point
[485](https://docs.rs#485)    Some(aligned_ptr - ptr)
[486](https://docs.rs#486)}
[487](https://docs.rs#487)
[488](https://docs.rs#488)/// Compute and validate offsets for a copy operation with the given parameters.
[489](https://docs.rs#489)fn compute_offsets<S: Slab>(
[490](https://docs.rs#490)    dst: &S,
[491](https://docs.rs#491)    start_offset: usize,
[492](https://docs.rs#492)    t_layout: Layout,
[493](https://docs.rs#493)    min_alignment: usize,
[494](https://docs.rs#494)) -> Result<CopyRecord, CopyError> {
[495](https://docs.rs#495)    let copy_layout = t_layout.align_to(min_alignment.next_power_of_two())?;
[496](https://docs.rs#496)
[497](https://docs.rs#497)    let copy_start_offset =
[498](https://docs.rs#498)        align_offset_up_to(dst.base_ptr() as usize, start_offset, copy_layout.align())
[499](https://docs.rs#499)            .ok_or(CopyError::InvalidLayout)?;
[500](https://docs.rs#500)    let copy_end_offset = copy_start_offset
[501](https://docs.rs#501)        .checked_add(copy_layout.size())
[502](https://docs.rs#502)        .ok_or(CopyError::InvalidLayout)?;
[503](https://docs.rs#503)    let copy_end_offset_padded = copy_start_offset
[504](https://docs.rs#504)        .checked_add(copy_layout.pad_to_align().size())
[505](https://docs.rs#505)        .ok_or(CopyError::InvalidLayout)?;
[506](https://docs.rs#506)
[507](https://docs.rs#507)    // check start is inside slab
[508](https://docs.rs#508)    // if within slab, we also know that copy_start_offset is <= isize::MAX since slab.size() must be <= isize::MAX
[509](https://docs.rs#509)    if copy_start_offset > dst.size() {
[510](https://docs.rs#510)        return Err(CopyError::OffsetOutOfBounds);
[511](https://docs.rs#511)    }
[512](https://docs.rs#512)
[513](https://docs.rs#513)    // check end is inside slab
[514](https://docs.rs#514)    if copy_end_offset_padded > dst.size() {
[515](https://docs.rs#515)        return Err(CopyError::OutOfMemory);
[516](https://docs.rs#516)    }
[517](https://docs.rs#517)
[518](https://docs.rs#518)    Ok(CopyRecord {
[519](https://docs.rs#519)        copy_start_offset,
[520](https://docs.rs#520)        copy_end_offset,
[521](https://docs.rs#521)        copy_end_offset_padded,
[522](https://docs.rs#522)    })
[523](https://docs.rs#523)}
[524](https://docs.rs#524)
[525](https://docs.rs#525)/// An error that may occur during a copy operation.
[526](https://docs.rs#526)#[derive(Debug)]
[527](https://docs.rs#527)pub enum CopyError {
[528](https://docs.rs#528)    /// Copy would exceed the end of the allocation
[529](https://docs.rs#529)    OutOfMemory,
[530](https://docs.rs#530)    /// Requested to copy to an offset outside the bounds of the allocation
[531](https://docs.rs#531)    OffsetOutOfBounds,
[532](https://docs.rs#532)    /// Computed invalid layout for copy operation, probably caused by incredibly large size, offset, or min-alignment parameters
[533](https://docs.rs#533)    InvalidLayout,
[534](https://docs.rs#534)}
[535](https://docs.rs#535)
[536](https://docs.rs#536)impl core::fmt::Display for CopyError {
[537](https://docs.rs#537)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
[538](https://docs.rs#538)        write!(f, "{}", match self {
[539](https://docs.rs#539)            Self::OutOfMemory => "Copy would exceed the end of the allocation",
[540](https://docs.rs#540)            Self::OffsetOutOfBounds => "Requested copy to a location starting outside the allocation",
[541](https://docs.rs#541)            Self::InvalidLayout => "Invalid layout, probably caused by incredibly large size, offset, or alignment parameters",
[542](https://docs.rs#542)        })
[543](https://docs.rs#543)    }
[544](https://docs.rs#544)}
[545](https://docs.rs#545)
[546](https://docs.rs#546)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[547](https://docs.rs#547)impl std::error::Error for CopyError {}
[548](https://docs.rs#548)
[549](https://docs.rs#549)impl From<LayoutError> for CopyError {
[550](https://docs.rs#550)    fn from(_err: LayoutError) -> Self {
[551](https://docs.rs#551)        Self::InvalidLayout
[552](https://docs.rs#552)    }
